actual.boundary: Fixed finite M and fixed n only. The theorem does not provide an M-uniform coefficient norm, n-to-infinity convergence, an all-order QPS sum, or physical lambda=1 control.
actual.count: A safe rooted ordered connected n-edge tuple count is (n!)^2 z^n: choose one of n! edge-growth orders, then at step j use at most jz incidences. Thus support is at most n+1 and diameter at most n. The count is deliberately nonoptimal.
actual.exact_assumptions: At fixed M on a finite connected zero-source Q3 spatial graph with deg(x)>=1, each onsite Ritz space is finite dimensional; H0=sum_x k_(x,M)>=0, P0=tensor_x P_x is the tensor product of onsite ground projectors, and every onsite excitation gap is at least Gamma. Choose omega_(x,e)>=0 on incident edges with sum_(e containing x) omega_(x,e)=1; on the periodic coordination-z graph use omega_(x,e)=1/z. For e={x,y}, define tilde B_(e,M)=B_(e,M)+delta_1[omega_(x,e)P_(1,x)+omega_(y,e)P_(1,y)], V_M=sum_e tilde B_(e,M), H_M(lambda)=sum_x k_(x,M)+lambda V_M, and J_M=max_x sum_(e containing x)||tilde B_(e,M)||. The onsite allocation identity sum_e delta_1[omega_(x,e)P_(1,x)+omega_(y,e)P_(1,y)]=delta_1 sum_x P_(1,x) makes H_M(1) exactly the physical zero-source fixed-M Q3 Hamiltonian up to the removed scalar. The onsite ground projector may have arbitrary finite rank, hence the Q3 rank-two P_x is allowed. The subtraction k=h_site-epsilon_0-delta_1 P_1 makes phi_0 and phi_1 exact zero modes of H0, while the allocated term restores their physical splitting at lambda=1. Constants may depend on M, J_M, ||k_M||/Gamma and degree.
actual.linked_theorem: For every fixed n, the multivariate standard-SW coefficient H_eff,n=sum_C K_(n,C) has K_(n,C)=0 unless C is connected and |C|<=n, and K_(n,C) acts only on the vertex support Lambda(C). This fixed-coefficient theorem needs no convergence of the full SW series.

rows.actual: This package preserves every v2.5 and earlier conclusion and issued field at its historical value. At zero source, BDL Theorem 2 gives connected standard-SW coefficients separately at every fixed order n and fixed finite Ritz cutoff M; it does not assert convergence of the full series. The volume-extensive energy approximation is separately for each fixed n, fixed M and sufficiently small scaled coupling |lambda|J_M, not automatically for physical lambda=1, uniformly in M, or as n tends to infinity. The zero-source Q3 result constructs and removes the Ritz cutoff only for the third- and fourth-order coefficients using the stated uniform relative-form block constants and finite-rank low-high legs. It is not a rank-two unbounded block diagonalization or an all-order construction, a convergent BCH/Lie-Schwinger series, a QPS phase transfer, or a phasewise GNS intertwiner. The first negative rejects deriving high-high insertions from the low-high tail alone; the second rejects deriving a commuting spatial local net from formal seed supports after temporal orbit smearing. Neither is a nonexistence theorem for stronger weighted cutoff hypotheses or for every orbit-smeared carrier. No actual all-shape or all-exhaustion Cauchy compatibility, all-exhaustion common alpha, identified generator or KMS quotient, exact oscillator two-phase QPS, broken-sector oscillator temporal mass or GNS gap, regulator removal, continuum, physical-empty comparison, Round-1, C6, CP1, physical Sector A, or Pre-A closure follows.
